title: The Japanese tour: hip audiences and copyist bands
summary: On the Orient trip Nat's love songs brought the house down, and Japanese bands copied Miller, Goodman and Herman perfectly.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x:
Yeah, it was always Buddy Cole who would always play the things on ... that was when we went to the Orient, it was quite a good experience; we did an hour and a half television show there, and it's funny how the language, you know, with music, language is no barrier. They just -- in Japan, they really loved him, you know, he was singing all these love songs, and they know every song that he would sing. He would start -- he would sing "Unforgettable", the house would come down, just like it would here, you know.

But the Japanese people are very, very hip, you know, to American music. Because while we were there, we would go to different clubs, and they had a band playing like Glenn Miller, and then you'd go to another club and you'd hear Benny Goodman, and you'd have Woodie Herman, and they played like them, you know? They played all their arrangements; they could, they could copy anything.
But they didn't have anybody singing like Nat, did they?

No, but they had that Beneke Tex Beneke. Oh yeah, and they could do it. You know, they don't invent too much, but I mean, they can copy. They are the best copyers in the world; anything you can think of, the things you by -- and they'll improve on anything someone else invents. So they
take it right through. Through everything.
